currentRules.title: No emoji in Core EM X post text or IG captions
currentRules.detail: Julian adds any emoji himself. Bots and drafts must ship with none. This replaced 'emoji optional, 0 to 2' later the same day.
currentRules.source: Julian 2026-11-26 (after the approved playbook; t271u / no-emoji rule)

currentRules.title: #TBT posts open with the clinical hook
currentRules.detail: The '#TBT Core EM Ep N (year) with Dr. Name' credit line sits on its own line just above the link. The year stays. A new first line may only restate a claim already in that post's approved text or the episode source; anything new goes to Claude for a fact-check first.

currentRules.title: Plain-topic first lines, not case vignettes
currentRules.detail: Name the clinical topic in line 1. Case vignettes and quizzes underdelivered in the peer sample (case lift 0.90, n=46).
currentRules.source: Engagement playbook 2026-11-25; adopted with hook-first rule, Julian 2026-11-26

currentRules.title: Card sets go out as one multi-image post
currentRules.detail: Up to 4 images in one post, never a reply thread. Core EM's August 2026 card thread: card 1 reached 1,609 views; cards 2 to 4 reached 125 to 236.

currentRules.title: No quote posts as the delivery for new content
currentRules.detail: Post new content as an original post. Originals beat quote posts in 7 of 8 peer accounts (lift 1.04 vs 0.84).

currentRules.title: 4-week timing test
currentRules.detail: From Thursday 2026-11-26 through Thursday 2026-12-24: X videos at 8:00 AM ET on Monday and Thursday; X card sets at 7:30 PM ET on Tuesday and Saturday. Write 'Post time: H:MM AM/PM ET' at the start of the row's Notes. Compare views and engagement to the November video baseline after Dec 24. This is a test, not a fixed rule. IG times are unchanged.

currentRules.title: Card post text adds new info and never repeats the cards
currentRules.detail: Read the cards before writing the X text. Useful text (a hook, the clinical why, a pitfall, or a pearl the cards leave out) or minimal text (a one-line hook plus the link).

currentRules.title: No em dashes in post text
currentRules.detail: Use plain punctuation. This applies to X post text and IG captions.

currentRules.title: Current video standard
currentRules.detail: Guest intro near the start with a name card when the episode has one. Every take-home is set up in the body, not only in the wrap-up. Every clip teaches the why. Signpost every splice. Badge-only logo, top-left. 1 to 3 word bottom captions, karaoke-style. Runtime may flex to about 5 minutes to cover take-homes.
currentRules.source: Julian 2026-11-08 LAST standard, plus 2026-11-12 guest-intro and 2026-11-13 teach-the-why / take-home rules (Sheet rules 9, 14, 17, 20, 21, 22)

currentRules.title: X videos in 4:5 with a caption band
currentRules.detail: New X video standard (format trial starting with the Ep 223 Thyroid Storm remake): 1080x1350 (4:5). Captions stay in the bottom 270 px band. The CORE EM badge stays top-left only. No pictorial logo on the end card. Deliver a Google Drive .mov (video/quicktime) so it opens on Julian's iPhone; a raw .mp4 often lands as application/mp4, which his phone cannot open. A 9:16 cut may still exist for Instagram.
currentRules.source: Julian 2026-11-26 (Ep 223 4:5 remake; Drive .mov lesson from Sheet rule 6 and the 2026-11-26 .mp4 upload)

currentRules.title: Instagram browser check before assuming a post was missed
currentRules.detail: When checking whether an Instagram post went out, open the public @core.em profile in a browser (read only, no engagement). Do not skip the check, and do not auto-reschedule only because a connector or a follower login could not see the account. If the check still fails, say so plainly. On 2026-11-26, Ep 222 LAST had already been posted by Julian on the original Wednesday 11-25 slot, but the row had been auto-rescheduled to Thursday 11-26 at 1:00 PM ET after the account could not be checked.
currentRules.source: Julian 2026-11-26 (he posted the LAST Reel himself and asked why it had not been checked)

priorRules.title: Emoji optional, 0 to 2 per post
priorRules.detail: Approved in the morning playbook pass (Sheet rule 48). Replaced later the same day by no emoji at all.

priorRules.title: 1 to 3 emojis in every post
priorRules.detail: Part of the 2026-11-24 copy-ready post format (Sheet rule 46, original wording). Replaced by 0 to 2 optional, then by none.

priorRules.title: #TBT posts opened with the credit line
priorRules.detail: Older-episode remakes flagged as a throwback with the episode year and #TBT, typically in the first line.
priorRules.source: Julian 2026-11-09 (Sheet rule 26), replaced by Sheet rule 49

priorRules.title: Card sets could go out as a reply thread
priorRules.detail: No set format until 2026-11-26. The August 2026 Superwarfarin-style card thread is the example of why this was dropped.

priorRules.title: No set posting time
priorRules.detail: Julian posted when he was free. Sheet rows had no Post time until the 4-week timing test.

priorRules.title: Target about 60 seconds for new shorts
Coherent 1 to 2 minute structured short
priorRules.detail: The LAST standard runtime. Later flexed to about 5 minutes when take-home coverage required it. People sometimes still describe the pre-flex standard as 90 to 120 seconds.

priorRules.title: X videos in 9:16 (1080x1920)
priorRules.detail: Posted November videos on @Core_EM were 1080x1920. The 4:5 (1080x1350) caption-band frame is the new X trial starting 2026-11-26.
priorRules.source: Public media on Nov 9-16 @Core_EM videos; Ep 223 remake 2026-11-26

evidence.title: Engagement analysis of daily EM and critical care X picks, plus @Core_EM

sample.accounts: 14 EM and critical care accounts with at least 8 posts in the window (18 tried; 4 had no posts in the window), plus 7 topic searches

evidence.headline: Core EM November videos converted viewers better than the peer set (median engagement rate 3.04% vs 1.18%, and 2.05 likes per 1,000 followers vs 0.45) but reached fewer people (median 1,659 impressions vs 3,481).

findings.finding: Video and multi-image posts beat single images and text-only posts from the same account.
findings.numbers: Median lift vs the account's own median: multi-image 1.64 (n=22), video 1.33 (n=47), single image 1.00 (n=149), text 1.00 (n=105). Held in 5 of 6 accounts that used both.
Pooled lift 1.04 for originals (n=228) vs 0.84 for quotes (n=106). Originals won in 7 of 8 accounts that did both.

findings.finding: 'What's new' posts travel and get saved.
findings.numbers: Guideline or new-evidence posts: lift 1.15 (n=54) and the highest bookmark-to-like ratio, 0.50. 6 of the 18 posts with 300+ likes were 2026 guideline or journal updates.

findings.finding: Reference posts built to be saved earn bookmarks close to likes.
findings.numbers: Reference or summary topics: lift 1.48 (n=17). Example: @cliffreid 3D heart tool, 1,186 likes, 1,381 bookmarks, 89,478 views.

findings.finding: First lines that name the topic plainly do best. Cases and quizzes underdeliver.
findings.numbers: 13 of the 18 posts with 300+ likes opened with a plain title or statement; 1 opened with a case. Case vignettes: lift 0.90 (n=46).

findings.finding: Posts with no line breaks underperform.
findings.numbers: No line breaks: lift 0.85 (n=63) vs 1.00 to 1.03 with breaks. Bookmark-to-like 0.10 vs 0.33 to 0.38.
findings.strength: Weak; Core EM already uses breaks

findings.finding: Timing: early morning, evening, and Monday are slightly better. Overnight, Wednesday, and Friday are worse.
findings.numbers: 6 to 9 AM ET lift 1.24 (n=39); 6 PM to midnight 1.31 (n=51); midnight to 6 AM 0.85 (n=42). Monday 1.31 (n=51), Wednesday 0.81 (n=37), Friday 0.87 (n=37).

findings.finding: Hashtags, links, and emoji show no consistent effect.
findings.numbers: Of the 18 posts with 300+ likes, 12 had no hashtags, 15 had no link, and 17 had no emoji. Within the same account, results split both ways.

findings.finding: Opinion posts about the profession got the biggest lift but almost no saves. They do not fit Core EM's brand.

caveats: Observational. Format, topic, and account habits overlap, so no pattern is proven to cause anything.
X search cannot filter by likes, so the 300+ set is small (18).
The API cut long posts off at 280 characters, so length, hashtag, and link counts are understated for long posts.
Newer posts were still collecting likes when read, which slightly understates late-November ones.
The Core EM November video sample is small (n=6), so Core EM-specific timing effects cannot be measured yet.
